nodes.label: Patient is a 27-year-old woman with occasional alcohol consumption and no history of viral hepatitis, steatohepatitis, autoimmune liver disease, or metabolic liver disease
Patient was taking axitinib, azelnidipine, and tramadol hydrochloride
After stopping alcohol and axitinib, hepatobiliary enzyme levels remained unchanged
Liver biopsy shows PAX8-positive malignant cell clusters invading Glisson's capsule, occluding interlobular veins, and destroying interlobular bile ducts
MRI shows a hypointense hepatic hilar region in the hepatobiliary phase
Imaging shows heterogeneous hepatic parenchyma with an isoechoic enhancing region extending from porta hepatis to right dorsal side
The hepatobiliary lesion is a PAX8-positive malignant infiltrative/metastatic process
Primary site of the PAX8-positive malignant process has not yet been identified
The hepatobiliary lesion is a metastasis from an extrahepatic PAX8-positive primary tumor
Hepatobiliary metastasis from an extrahepatic PAX8-positive primary tumor
Axitinib is a targeted therapy primarily used for advanced renal cell carcinoma
Extended immunohistochemistry and PET-CT have not been performed
Retrieval attempts have not identified an extrahepatic primary site
PAX8 is characteristically expressed in renal cell carcinoma, Müllerian tumors, and thyroid tumors
The hepatobiliary lesion is a metastasis from a renal cell carcinoma
